FR-001.title: The application MUST record each logical player connection with a timestamp, application-run identifier, stable logical-session identifier, and resolved role.

FR-002.title: The application MUST record each logical player disconnection exactly once with the same logical-session identifier and its last known role.

FR-003.title: The application MUST record every effective role transition with the logical-session identifier and the previous and new roles.

FR-004.title: The application MUST record each command request accepted for Overseer review with a unique correlation identifier, requesting logical session, current role, terminal identifier, and safe command identifier.

FR-005.title: The application MUST record each approval or decline with the originating request correlation identifier, decision, and resulting execution outcome when applicable.

FR-006.title: Duplicate, superseded, invalid, or execution-failed command requests MUST be distinguishable through safe outcome categories without recording raw command content or output.

FR-007.title: The application MUST record hacking puzzle start, accepted or rejected interaction, dud-removal, attempt-replenishment, success, failure, reset, and interruption events when those events occur.

FR-008.title: Each hacking record MUST include the application-run identifier, puzzle correlation identifier, terminal identifier, acting logical session and role when available, event category, and safe outcome metadata applicable to that event.

FR-009.title: Hacking records MUST NOT contain candidate words, the correct password, memory-board content, or other data that can reveal the puzzle solution.

FR-010.title: Required runtime records MUST use consistent event categories, timestamps, severity, and correlation fields so connection, command, and puzzle flows can be reconstructed in order.

FR-011.title: Development runs and supported release packages MUST retain the same required runtime-event coverage in a stable per-user location outside application installation files.

FR-012.title: The Overseer interface MUST provide a log access action that opens or reveals the current retained-log location without requiring a development terminal.

FR-013.title: When the operating system cannot open or reveal the retained-log location, the application MUST show a safe actionable error that includes the exact intended location.

FR-014.title: Retained logs MUST distinguish application runs and preserve at least the current and immediately previous run after both clean and unexpected shutdown, subject to bounded retention.

FR-015.title: Retention MUST impose a documented finite storage boundary and remove older log data without deleting or blocking the active log.

FR-016.title: Logging or retained-storage failures MUST NOT change player authority, command decisions, puzzle behavior, application lifecycle ordering, or existing user-visible results.

FR-017.title: Retained records MUST exclude provider tokens, player and generated passwords, character names, session and terminal content, command output, puzzle solution data, and unredacted private dependency errors.

FR-018.title: Automated checks MUST cover connection and role transitions, command request decisions and exceptional outcomes, hacking lifecycle events, packaged-log access, retention, fallback behavior, and forbidden-value redaction.

SC-005.title: A high-volume retention test remains within the documented storage boundary while preserving a writable, identifiable active log.

context: area: application logging and composition boundaries
area: player coordination, command approval, and hacking runtime
area: packaged per-user application data and Overseer access
constraint: retain safe identifiers while excluding secrets and gameplay content
intent: Give the Overseer a safe, correlated runtime record of player, command-decision, and hacking activity that remains accessible from installed releases.
approach: Compose one run-scoped retained writer behind the existing application logger, emit safe audit facts from authoritative coordination transitions through the existing effect router, and expose one protobuf-governed Overseer action for opening the fixed app-owned log directory. Keep public player contracts and gameplay state unchanged.

decisions.decision: Retain text logs through one bounded standard-library writer attached to the existing logger
decisions.why: Preserves the pinned logger and development output while adding packaged persistence and deterministic rotation
decisions.rejected: Replacing the logger, file-only packaged logging, or an external rotation dependency

decisions.decision: Produce allowlisted audit facts in coordinator order and format them only at the root
decisions.why: The coordinator owns logical presence, authority, pending approvals, and private puzzle identity
decisions.rejected: Transport-level connection logs, projection-only diffs, or injecting the concrete logger into control

decisions.decision: Use a closed event and field vocabulary that excludes names, content, targets, solutions, credentials, and raw errors
decisions.why: Creates a testable redaction boundary before any diagnostic value reaches a writer
decisions.rejected: Logging complete commands or snapshots and redacting only at final output

decisions.decision: Expose a no-argument private OpenLogLocation action for the fixed app-owned directory
decisions.why: Makes packaged logs reachable without granting arbitrary filesystem or file-URL access
decisions.rejected: Broadening OpenURL, building an embedded viewer, or exposing access to players

decisions.decision: Use deterministic target-aware checks everywhere and optional matching-host packaged UI evidence
decisions.why: Proves portable package separation while honoring the constitution native-evidence rule
decisions.rejected: Requiring unavailable native UI automation on every release target or testing development only

decisions.decision: Permit a completed Companion spec to reopen only for newly appended unchecked convergence tasks
decisions.why: Convergence added T026-T032 after the original implement step had shipped; a numbered, idempotent implement/convergence substep preserves the append-only lifecycle and closes automatically when all tasks are journaled.
decisions.rejected: Hand-editing lifecycle JSON, reopening archived specs, or silently ignoring post-completion convergence tasks.

decisions.decision: Prune retained segments to one below the configured maximum before creating a new segment.
decisions.why: A cleanup failure then prevents admission instead of leaving a newly created segment beyond the finite boundary; rotation degrades once to fallback with no further growth.
decisions.rejected: Create first and treat post-creation cleanup failure as a warning.

decisions.decision: Make the retained writer the sole owner of storage-degradation warnings
decisions.why: The production root composes the still-usable writer without logging its initialization error again, guaranteeing one safe warning through the fallback
decisions.rejected: Logging the same initialization failure in both diagnostics.Open and runApplication

decisions.decision: Treat retained segment ordinals as decimal strings of at least three digits
decisions.why: This preserves every existing filename while keeping all future generated ordinals recognizable and prunable after 999
decisions.rejected: Increasing to another fixed width or wrapping the ordinal, which would only delay the boundary or risk filename collisions

plan.key_finding: Logical connection, role, command, and puzzle evidence must originate in the serialized coordinator; transport logs or public-state diffs cannot provide correct correlation.
